thread:
lin: quick ask — i'm seeing a burst of prefix-cache evictions in prod during nightly traffic spikes. can someone run a focused benchmark to try to reproduce? i suspect fragmentation + our prefetch heuristic is triggering evictions under medium concurrency.

lin: target workload: long-seq generation (avg seq ~1500), mix of repeating prefixes, 60% cacheable prefixes. goal: get per-shard eviction counts, occupancy histogram, and per-prefix lifetime distribution.

lin: suggested command to run (kvbench):
```
./tools/kvbench --model redwood-v1 --seq 2048 --concurrency 48 --duration 180 \\
  --workload mix:0.6:repeat_prefix --kv-prefetch=on --kv-prefetch-window=64 \\
  --kv-sample-rate=0.1 --emit-metrics=evictions,occupancy,prefix-lifetime
```

lin: please run on a medium-size node image (p4d-sim or a100-sim) and post logs + flamegraphs. tagging this to get eyes: @sarah @raj @mike :eyes:

sarah: on it. i'll run against the a100 sim and a g4dn-small to compare memory pressure. will post flamegraphs.

raj: quick note — when you enable kv-prefetch-window=64 we sometimes see a transient burst of cache fills that looks like fragmentation; add `--kv-coalesce=1` as a control to see if coalescing kills the churn.

mike: fwiw PR #4987 changes the eviction backoff timer; if the benchmark reproduces it, we should try with/without that patch. i can spin a job with the pre-PR binary.

sarah: ran a100 sim job, short summary: eviction spikes ~t+45s after start, ownership churn across shards 2 & 3. hit-rate drops from 92% -> 67% during the spike. uploading artifacts: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/bench/1765426789/a100-flame.html and logs: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/bench/1765426789/a100.log :thumbsup:

lin: awesome, thanks. can you paste the small eviction summary here? a single line per-shard helps.

sarah: shard0 evicted=12 occupancy=78% avg-lifetime=12.4s
sarah: shard1 evicted=9 occupancy=81% avg-lifetime=13.1s
sarah: shard2 evicted=143 occupancy=45% avg-lifetime=3.6s <-- hot
sarah: shard3 evicted=138 occupancy=47% avg-lifetime=3.9s <-- hot

raj: that pattern screams hotset shift + fragmentation. low occupancy but high eviction suggests small objects without coalescing. try `--kv-sample-type=prefix-frag` to get per-prefix fragment counts.

mike: started a control run with pre-PR binary + `--kv-coalesce=1` on g4dn. I'll put logs in the same s3 path with suffix prepr-coalesce.

dev-bot: bench-runner started job 1765426812 on instance g4dn.xlarge (user=mike)

mike: control run results (short): hit-rate stays ~90%, evicted shard2=4 shard3=3, occupancy stable. looks promising. logs: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/bench/1765426789/g4dn-prepr-coalesce.log

lin: interesting — so coalescing + pre-PR backoff reduces churn. this suggests the combination of newer backoff + no-coalesce is the regression.

lin: next steps: 1) raj to add per-prefix fragmentation telemetry (kv-exporter change) 2) mike to open rollback/patch candidate for the backoff tweak 3) sarah to run a focused long-duration job (~1hr) on prod-like traffic.

raj: i'll draft telemetry change and add a lightweight sampling endpoint so we don't blow prometheus. will open a tiny PR today.

mike: drafting rollback PR now, will tag runtime and eng-sre for quick review.

sarah: scheduling the 1hr job for tonight 02:00 UTC — will watch for evictions and alert if >50/s sustained.

ops-bot: scheduled job for 2026-03-12T02:00:00Z (job id 1765500000)

lin: perfect. thanks everyone. once we have the 1hr run and the telemetry PR we can decide to revert or tweak coalesce/backoff defaults. cc @eng-oncall

mike: pinging reviewers on the rollback PR shortly. :bell:

lin: if anyone else wants to reproduce locally, here's a minimal reproduction (low-cost):
```
# low-cost reproduce (short)
./tools/kvbench --model redwood-small --seq 1024 --concurrency 24 --duration 90 \\
  --workload mix:0.6:repeat_prefix --kv-prefetch=on --kv-prefetch-window=64 \\
  --kv-coalesce=0 --kv-sample-rate=0.05
```

sarah: thanks, running local reproduce now to validate before the night job.

mike: noted that we should also include a metric for `prefetch_inflight` in dashboards — adding to follow-up ticket.

lin: created ticket INF-762: investigate prefix fragmentation regression + telemetry, linking artifacts and PRs.

sarah: all set here, will report back after the long run. :rocket:
